source.title: [re:DEFINICIJA] mons. Vlado Košić: Javna molitva krunice je proročki znak vremena (ep. 6)

summary.title_hr: [re:DEFINICIJA] mons. Vlado Košić: Javna molitva krunice je proročki znak vremena (ep. 6)
summary.abstract_hr: U 6. epizodi podcasta Redefinicija gost je mons. Vlado Košić, biskup sisački i bivši pomoćni biskup zagrebački. Govori o odrastanju u Družbincu kraj Varaždina, svećeničkom pozivu i službi župnika na prvoj crti u Domovinskom ratu na Banovini. Opisuje imenovanje pomoćnim biskupom 1999., poslijeratnu i poslijepotresnu obnovu crkava u Sisačkoj biskupiji te svoju ljubav prema Mariji i mariologiji. Javnu molitvu krunice muškaraca smatra proročkim znakom vremena, a podršku Hodu za život ne vidi kao politiku nego kao moralnu obvezu zaštite života. Govori i o blaženom Alojziju Stepincu, za kojeg vjeruje da će ga papa Lav proglasiti svetim, te o svojim knjigama i talentima.
key_topics: biskupska služba i obnova crkava nakon potresa
medijski napadi i odnos prema laičkim pokretima
key_points: Košić je rođen u Varaždinu, a odrastao je u Družbincu u župi Petrijanec. Djetinjstvo opisuje kao sretno, a želja za svećeništvom javila mu se još dok je kao dijete postao ministrant.
Tijekom Domovinskog rata bio je župnik Hrastovice, a zatim Petrinje. Tri je godine živio uz kapelu u Mošćenici na prvoj crti, a te je događaje opisao u knjizi Župnik na prvoj crti.
Za pomoćnog biskupa zagrebačkog zaređen je 6. veljače 1999., s nepunih 40 godina. Imenovanje je doživio kao teško iskušenje i križ koji je prihvatio.
Nakon potresa Sisačka biskupija obnavlja ili gradi 52 crkvena objekta, od čega 28 župnih crkava. Dovršeno je 16 objekata, a obnova bi mogla trajati još dvije do tri godine.
Javnu molitvu krunice muškaraca smatra proročkim znakom vremena: odgovorni katolički muževi vide da svijet srlja u propast i u Mariji vide ruku spasa. Na molitvi nije vidio ništa protivno Crkvi.
Podršku Hodu za život ne smatra političkim djelovanjem, nego kršćanskom i moralnom obvezom zaštite života od začeća do prirodne smrti.

Blaženog Alojzija Stepinca smatra svojim zaštitnikom i vjeruje da će ga papa Lav proglasiti svetim. Ističe da je Stepinac spašavao i srpsku, odnosno kozaračku, i židovsku djecu te da istina u dijalogu sa Srpskom pravoslavnom crkvom ne smije biti žrtvovana.
key_topics_en: episcopal ministry and church reconstruction after the earthquake
media attacks and relationship with lay movements
key_points_en: Košić was born in Varaždin, and grew up in Družbinec in the parish of Petrijanec. He describes his childhood as happy, and the desire for the priesthood arose in him when he became an altar server as a child.

During the Homeland War he was the parish priest of Hrastovica, and then of Petrinja. For three years he lived next to the chapel in Mošćenica on the front lines, and he described those events in the book Parish Priest on the Front Line.
He was ordained an auxiliary bishop of Zagreb on February 6, 1999, at barely 40 years of age. He experienced the appointment as a difficult trial and a cross that he accepted.

Following the earthquake, the Diocese of Sisak is reconstructing or building 52 church buildings, of which 28 are parish churches. 16 buildings have been completed, and the reconstruction could last another two to three years.

He considers the men's public Rosary prayer a prophetic sign of the times: responsible Catholic men see that the world is rushing into ruin and in Mary they see a saving hand. At the prayer, he did not see anything contrary to the Church.
He does not consider support for the Walk for Life to be political activity, but a Christian and moral obligation to protect life from conception until natural death.

He considers Blessed Alojzije Stepinac to be his patron and believes that Pope Leo will canonize him as a saint. He emphasizes that Stepinac saved both Serbian, that is Kozara, and Jewish children, and that the truth in dialogue with the Serbian Orthodox Church must not be sacrificed.
summary.title_en: [re:DEFINICIJA] Msgr. Vlado Košić: Public Rosary Prayer Is a Prophetic Sign of the Times (ep. 6)
summary.abstract_en: In the 6th episode of the Redefinicija podcast, the guest is Msgr. Vlado Košić, Bishop of Sisak and former Auxiliary Bishop of Zagreb. He speaks about growing up in Družbinec near Varaždin, his priestly vocation, and his service as a parish priest on the front lines during the Homeland War in Banovina. He describes his appointment as auxiliary bishop in 1999, the post-war and post-earthquake reconstruction of churches in the Diocese of Sisak, and his love for Mary and mariology. He considers the men's public Rosary prayer to be a prophetic sign of the times, and he sees support for the Walk for Life not as politics but as a moral obligation to protect life. He also speaks about Blessed Alojzije Stepinac, whom he believes Pope Leo will canonize as a saint, as well as about his books and talents.
